CausalChain: Inflammatory signals in HCC → increased IL-6 production → activation of STAT3 in tumor cells → STAT3-driven transcriptional upregulation of AFP → secreted AFP interacts with IL-6 receptor complex or downregulates SOCS → enhanced IL-6/STAT3 signaling → promotion of cancer stem cell features, drug resistance, and immune evasion.
Hypothesis: AFP is not merely a diagnostic marker in HCC but actively enhances IL-6/STAT3 signaling through a positive feedback loop; thus, interrupting AFP’s interaction with IL-6/STAT3 pathway components may reduce tumor aggressiveness and overcome drug resistance in hepatocellular carcinoma.
Abstract: In hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), the interleukin‐6/STAT3 axis plays a central role in promoting tumorigenesis, immune escape, and drug resistance. While alpha‐fetoprotein (AFP) is conventionally used as a biomarker for HCC, emerging data suggest that AFP may have active roles in modulating intracellular signaling. Here, we propose a novel hypothesis wherein AFP functions as an autocrine amplifier of IL‐6/STAT3 signaling in HCC. In this model, elevated IL‐6 production in the tumor microenvironment activates STAT3, which in turn upregulates AFP expression. Secreted AFP then reinforces IL‐6/STAT3 pathway activation, either through direct interaction with receptor components or by modulating negative regulators such as SOCS proteins. This positive feedback loop may contribute to increased cancer stem cell renewal, enhanced epithelial–mesenchymal transition, and resistance to conventional therapies. Targeting AFP’s putative modulatory effects on the IL‐6/STAT3 axis could represent a novel therapeutic opportunity for improving HCC treatment outcomes.
